claims.text: Role in pheo: preop alternative: doxazosin 1 to 32 mg PO QD;
claims.quote: doxazosin 1 to 32 mg orally once daily

claims.text: doxazosin may be equally effective but better tolerated;
claims.quote: Some alpha-blockers, such as doxazosin, may be equally effective but better tolerated.

claims.text: start a BB only after adequate alpha-blockade.
claims.quote: Beta-blockers should not be used until adequate alpha-blockade has been achieved.

claims.text: Doxazosin (Cardura) safety: CI: hypersensitivity to doxazosin, other quinazolines (e.g., prazosin, terazosin), or any of its components.
claims.quote: The use of CARDURA is contraindicated in patients with a hypersensitivity to doxazosin, other quinazolines (e.g., prazosin, terazosin), or any of its components.

claims.text: Postural hypotension w/ or w/o symptoms (e.g., dizziness) may develop within a few hours after dosing; potential for syncope, esp after the initial dose or a dose increase.
claims.quote: Postural hypotension with or without symptoms (e.g., dizziness) may develop within a few hours following administration of CARDURA. However, infrequently, symptomatic postural hypotension has also been reported later than a few hours after dosing. As with other alpha-blockers, there is a potential for syncope, especially after the initial dose or after an increase in dosage strength.

claims.text: Concomitant PDE-5 inhibitor can result in additive BP lowering and symptomatic hypotension.
claims.quote: Concomitant administration of CARDURA with a PDE-5 inhibitor can result in additive blood pressure lowering effects and symptomatic hypotension.

claims.text: IFIS observed during cataract surgery in some pts on or previously treated w/ alpha1 blockers.
claims.quote: Intraoperative Floppy Iris Syndrome (IFIS) has been observed during cataract surgery in some patients on or previously treated with alpha1 blockers.

claims.text: No apparent benefit of stopping alpha1 blocker therapy b4 cataract surgery.
claims.quote: There does not appear to be a benefit of stopping alpha1 blocker therapy prior to cataract surgery.

claims.text: Rule out prostate cancer b4 starting therapy for BPH.
claims.quote: Carcinoma of the prostate should therefore be ruled out prior to commencing therapy with CARDURA for the treatment of BPH.

claims.text: Priapism (painful erection sustained for hours, unrelieved by intercourse or masturbation) associated w/ doxazosin; can lead to permanent impotence if not promptly treated.
claims.quote: Alpha1 antagonists, including doxazosin, have been associated with priapism (painful penile erection, sustained for hours and unrelieved by sexual intercourse or masturbation). This condition can lead to permanent impotence if not promptly treated.

claims.text: Strong CYP3A inhibitors may ↑ doxazosin exposure and risk of hypotension; monitor BP and for hypotension symptoms.
claims.quote: Strong CYP3A inhibitors may increase exposure to doxazosin. Monitor blood pressure and for symptoms of hypotension when CARDURA is used concomitantly with strong CYP3A inhibitors

claims.text: Severe hepatic impairment (Child-Pugh Class C) not recommended; monitor BP and hypotension symptoms in Child-Pugh Class A and B.
claims.quote: Use of CARDURA in patients with severe hepatic impairment (Child-Pugh Class C) is not recommended. Monitor blood pressure and for symptoms of hypotension in patients with lesser degrees of hepatic impairment (Child-Pugh Class A and B)

claims.text: Following the initial dose and each dose increase, monitor BP for at least 6 h.
claims.quote: Following the initial dose and with each dose increase of CARDURA, monitor blood pressure for at least 6 hours following administration.

claims.text: If discontinued for several days, restart therapy using the initial dosing regimen.
claims.quote: If CARDURA administration is discontinued for several days, therapy should be restarted using the initial dosing regimen.

claims.text: Most commonly reported adverse reactions: fatigue, malaise, hypotension, and dizziness.
claims.quote: The most commonly reported adverse reactions from clinical trials are fatigue, malaise, hypotension, and dizziness.

claims.text: OD: most likely manifestation is hypotension; usual treatment is IV fluid infusion; dialysis not indicated (highly protein bound).
claims.quote: The most likely manifestation of overdosage would be hypotension, for which the usual treatment would be intravenous infusion of fluid. As doxazosin is highly protein bound, dialysis would not be indicated.
